predecessors.name: Nawabs of Bengal

successors.name: British Raj

ledger.x: October 1755: Frederiksnagore is established at Serampore.
1 January 1756: the Nicobars are declared Danish property as Frederiksoerne.

ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 1763: the British leave Serampore after a year (the page gives no month).
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 1777: the colony passes from the Danish East India Company to the Crown.
1801: the British occupy Dansborg (Tranquebar), with Balasore and Frederiksnagore: 'British occupation 1801-1802'.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 1801: the British occupy Frederiksnagore (Serampore); the page gives no day.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 1802: the first British occupation of Frederiksnagore ends; the page gives the occupation as 1801-1802 and no day.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 17 August 1802: a letter cited by the page reports the Danish flag hoisted again on Tranquebar's fort.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 1808: the British occupy Frederiksnagore (Serampore) a second time (the page gives 1808-1815 for Dansborg, Balasore and Frederiksnagore, no month).
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)
British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 1815: the second British occupation of Frederiksnagore ends (the page gives 1808-1815 and no day).
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)
British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 1845: Tranquebar is sold to Britain: 'Tranquebar and most minor settlements sold' (no day on the page); the Tharangambadi page: 'Along with the Danish settlement of Serampore in Bengal, it was sold to the British in 1845.'
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 11 October 1845: Serampore is sold to Britain: 'On 11 October 1845, Serampore was sold to Britain.'
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 1869: Danish India ends (infobox 'Established 1620 / disestablished 1869'): the Nicobars are formally annexed by Britain, which 'made them part of British India' (Nicobar Islands page).

wars.name: British occupation of Danish India, 1801-1802
wars.outcome: The British occupy Dansborg, Balasore and Frederiksnagore; the Danish flag is hoisted again at Tranquebar on 17 August 1802.

wars.name: British occupation of Danish India, 1808-1815
wars.outcome: Occupied in the Napoleonic Wars (Tranquebar in February 1808); the Kiel peace treaty of 14 January 1814 restores them and sovereignty is transferred at Tranquebar on 20 September 1815.

certainty.note: The pages give no bounds for Tranquebar (one village and a fort) or Serampore (three named villages), so both are drawn as small circles; the Nicobar coasts are natural limits.
